Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

the rest noun and adjective

what is left of something

also the rest of, the remainder, the rest of the day, as for the rest

classical

Liv. 21.33.1: agmen reliquum
Cato Agr. 2.4: quae reliqua opera sient

reliquus, reliqua, reliquum

adjective, agreeing with its noun

the rest of, the remaining

Latin puts the adjective with its noun: agmen reliquum, the rest of the column. Lewis & Short: reliquus is what remains of a thing; cēterī the others besides those named. “As for the rest”: quod reliquum est (Cic. Att. 16.15.3, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • reliquum, reliquī n. + gen. — the rest of (a time, a quantity)

    noun with a partitive genitive · also used · classical · Liv. 2.25.2: reliquum diēī (Lewis & Short); Liv. 39.13: ubi reliquum vītae dēgere tūtō posset (Lewis & Short)

    The rest of the day, of one’s life: reliquum diēī, reliquum vītae.

  • cētera, cēterōrum n. pl. — the rest, everything else

    adjective used as a noun · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.4.1: cētera cōram agēmus; Cic. Fam. 7.18.2: cētera bellē

    In letters and talk: cētera cōram, the rest when we meet. As an accusative of respect, “in other respects”: cētera laetus (Hor. Ep. 1.10.50).

Examples

  • prīmā deinde lūce castra mōta et agmen reliquum incēdere coepit

    then at first light the camp was struck and the rest of the column began to moveLiv. 21.33.1

  • ubi cognita aequō animō sient quae reliqua opera sient, cūrārī utī perficiantur

    when he has calmly found out what work is left, let him see that it gets finishedCato Agr. 2.4

  • cētera cōram agēmus. haec properantēs scrīpsimus.

    we’ll deal with the rest face to face. I have written this in a hurry.Cic. Att. 4.4.1

  • cētera bellē; illud mīror

    the rest is fine; one thing surprises meCic. Fam. 7.18.2

  • cētera plāna, prōclīvia fore

    the rest of the way would be level or downhillLiv. 21.35.9

  • tōta quidem pōnātur anas, sed pectore tantum et cervīce sapit: cētera redde cocō

    serve the duck whole, by all means; but only the breast and neck have any taste: give the rest back to the cookMart. 13.52.1–2

See also the others, remain, everything, else.
